main_text.p: quæ partim ex ea, quam διοικήσεως[?] vocatam jam dixi, sumebatur jubente populo, partim ex tributis belli causa imperatis conficiebatur. Quæ si usum suum retinere potuisset, meliore loco, ut credere ratio suadet, fortuna reipu-blicæ Atticæ mansisset. Verum culpâ Periclis, ut perhibent historiæ, viri cæ-teroqui præstantissimi, ad demerendam gratiam plebis, in usum theatri maxi-mam partem conversa, rem militarem, qua steterat creveratque eousque reipu-blicæ fortuna, deteriorem, & cives in-ertiores fecit: inde fortunæ ruina se-cuta: quæ infra dicentur commodius &c plenius. Cum novo autem instituto, quo exhaustum ærarium militare fuit, novi quoque quæstores sunt orti, quos ἐπὶ τῶν θεωρικῶν ταμίας[?] nuncuparunt: quorum hoc munus erat, ut theatrum ingredi, & spectare cupienti tenuiori plebi, quæ & numerosissima, & spe-ctandi avidissima erat, totos dies in theatris residens, binos obolos elargi-retur. Satis de quæstoribus. Non solum autem hi, sed omnes omnino magi-stratus, & quotquot reipublicæ partem iquâ[?] administrabant, quotannis red-dendis rationibus erant obnoxii apud ἐφόρους[?] & apud ἀθηναίους[?]. Hos ut no-minibus

page.notes: Printed text is in one column, so the whole page is one paragraph continued from the previous page. Greek words in the line beginning "ἐπὶ" and the line beginning "ἐφόρους" are doubtful; the Greek there is faint and partly hidden by the margin rule. "iquâ" in the line "iquâ administrabant" is doubtful. The word "&c" is printed as shown. Faint marks at the left margin beside the lines "&c plenius", "quo exhaustum" and "ἐπὶ" are not legible text and are not transcribed. A small mark at the bottom left is a stamp or edge mark, not printed text, and is left out. Spellings were changed only for u/v, i/j and long s, as the rules require: "nouo" became "novo", "fuum" became "suum", "fi" became "si", "steterat" became "steterat".
